Language: en

OpenAnimalNutrition

The official URL for this implementation guide is: 

https://openanimalnutrition.org/fhir/animal-nutrition/ImplementationGuide/openanimalnutrition.fhir.animalnutrition

A FHIR Implementation Guide for representing and verifying the nutritional adequacy of an animal diet against published requirement standards (NRC, AAFCO, FEDIAF), expressed on a common mathematical basis. Species-agnostic by design; v0.1 binds canine and feline coverage. This guide models the adequacy VERDICT, not the means of producing a passing diet.

resource.name: Adequacy Interpretation
resource.description: Per-nutrient and overall interpretations of a diet's nutrient levels against the applied requirement standard. The rules for `deficient` and `excess` are stated, proposed and pending ratification, on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Adequacy Interpretation Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Adequacy Interpretation code system.

resource.name: Adult-maintenance adequacy under a 25% caloric restriction, canine, vs NRC
resource.description: A dog fed 25% less energy than it needs, checked against NRC's recommended allowances for adult dogs at maintenance, under the caloric-restriction rule proposed, pending ratification, on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page. Calcium at 1.2 g/Mcal meets NRC's minimum of 1 g/Mcal, but the restriction raises the minimum to 4/3 g/Mcal (recorded as 1.3333333, at 7 decimal places), so calcium is deficient. The overall verdict shown is illustrative: how it follows from the per-nutrient results is an open point on that page.

resource.name: Adult-maintenance adequacy, canine, vs AAFCO
resource.description: Adequacy of a canine adult-maintenance diet against AAFCO, with one nutrient under an authoritative maximum (calcium) and one under a derived-provisional ceiling (potassium). The overall verdict shown is illustrative: how it follows from the per-nutrient results is an open point on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Animal Nutrient Adequacy Assessment
resource.description:
The result of the agnostic, mathematical check of a diet's resolved nutrient
profile against a selected requirement standard (NRC / AAFCO / FEDIAF) for a
given species and life stage.

Each assessed nutrient is a component carrying the diet's level, the applicable
min/max requirement range, the common-basis decile expression, and a
per-nutrient interpretation. The decile expression is computed as stated,
proposed and pending ratification, on the
[Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page. The top-level
interpretation is the overall complete-and-balanced verdict.

Ratio nutrients such as Ca:P are components like any other nutrient, with a
unitless quantity (UCUM `1`). Non-linear ratio nutrients are excluded from the
component model by design.

A component's interpretation is `excess` only when the value is above an
authoritative maximum, one set by a standards body for the animal and the use
it is applied to (maxProvenance
`authoritative`), and not below a minimum set by the applied standard,
including one raised for a caloric restriction or by the AAFCO dry matter
factor (below). Above a conditional, template-set or derived-provisional
maximum, and not below the minimum, the interpretation stays `adequate`. The
band is then `range-d10` ("Highest (90% of Range or
Greater)"), which alone does not show that the maximum was exceeded:
referenceRange.high holds the maximum, and maxProvenance says what kind it is.

Where a caloric restriction, or the AAFCO dry matter factor for a food below
4 kcal/g of dry matter, raises a minimum set by the applied standard,
referenceRange.low holds the raised minimum, and the band is computed from it.
A value below it is `deficient`, even if it meets the minimum that applies
with no adjustment. A verdict checked under a caloric restriction above 0 records the
percentage in `caloricRestriction`. This rule, the condition on `excess` above,
and which minimums they cover are stated, proposed and pending ratification, on
the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

`performer` is optional. When a veterinarian, nutritionist or clinic ran or
reviewed the check, name them (Practitioner, PractitionerRole or Organization).
The organization that only operates the checking software is not the performer
unless it also reviewed this verdict. Software cannot be the performer of an
Observation in FHIR R5 (`performer` does not accept a Device). When software
computed the verdict, record it in `device`: a Device whose `name` and
`version` give the software's name and version, so a reader can tell which
checker, and which version of it, produced the verdict.

SCOPE: this profile models the VERDICT. Ingredient selection, fortification,
and rounding (i.e. how a passing diet is produced) are out of scope by design.

resource.name: Animal Nutrients (STUB)
resource.description: STUB. Populate from the canonical nutrient list; map to SNOMED-vet / LOINC where possible. Ratio nutrients (e.g. Ca:P) need explicit handling, and non-linear ratios are excluded from the component model by design (see the [Animal Nutrient Adequacy Assessment](StructureDefinition-animal-nutrient-adequacy.html) profile). Which ratios count as non-linear is an open point on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Animal Nutrients Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Animal Nutrients code system (a stub in v0.1).

resource.name: Animal Species (STUB)
resource.description: STUB. v0.1 implemented coverage only. TODO: bind to an external species value set.

resource.name: Animal Species Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Animal Species code system (a stub in v0.1).

resource.name: Applied Requirement Standard
resource.description: Which published requirement standard the adequacy check was run against, by its edition's code when the edition is known (for example AAFCO-2026). A variable selection, never hardcoded into the check.

resource.name: Caloric Restriction
resource.description:
The intentional caloric restriction that the check was run under, as a
percentage of the animal's energy need, in UCUM `%`: 25 means that the animal
is fed 25% less energy than it needs. Most of the applied standard's per-Mcal
minimums are then multiplied by 1 ÷ (1 − restriction ÷ 100) (under an AAFCO
selection, together with any AAFCO dry matter factor), so a nutrient can be
`deficient` although it meets the minimum that applies with no restriction.
The source template accepts 0 (none) or a number from 1 to 55. Present only
for a restriction above 0, and absent when none was entered (blank or 0 in the
template). An intake
entered in place of the calculated energy requirement is not a restriction.
Neither it nor the template's figure for how far it falls below that
requirement (cell N4 on the template's Standards tab) is recorded here. Which
minimums are raised, and the rule that makes a value below them `deficient`,
are stated, proposed and pending ratification, on the
[Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Example canine patient
resource.description: A dog, with species carried by the R5 patient-animal extension.

resource.name: Example checking software
resource.description: A placeholder for the software that computed the verdict, with its name and version.

resource.name: Example veterinarian
resource.description: A placeholder veterinarian who ran or reviewed the check.

resource.name: Life Stage
resource.description: The life stage whose requirements were applied (e.g. growth, adult maintenance). A variable selection.

resource.name: Life Stages
resource.description: Life stages for which requirement standards set nutrient requirements.

resource.name: Life Stages Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Life Stages code system.

resource.name: Maximum Provenance
resource.description:
The kind of maximum a nutrient's range high is: AUTHORITATIVE (set by a standards body for the animal and the use it is applied
to), CONDITIONAL (a standard's figure with a condition the check
does not verify), TEMPLATE-SET (set or computed by the source template) or
DERIVED-PROVISIONAL (computed by a disclosed rule from the minimum). Only a
value above an authoritative maximum is `excess`. How the source template's
maximum types map to these codes is stated, proposed and pending ratification,
on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

Derived ceilings prioritize consistency and determinism, NOT toxicological
calibration, and are revisable by the governance body. This flag exists so a
consumer can see at a glance which ceilings are authoritative and which are
not.

resource.name: Maximum Provenance Codes
resource.description: The kind of maximum a nutrient's range high is, which decides whether a value above it can be `excess`: only an authoritative maximum can. How the source template's maximum types map to these codes is stated, proposed and pending ratification, under Maximum types on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Maximum Provenance Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Maximum Provenance Codes code system.

resource.name: Nutrient Decile (Common-Basis Expression)
resource.description: The diet's level for this nutrient on the common mathematical basis used to compare across standards, expressed as a band of the Dynamic Decile System: four bands below the minimum and ten deciles from the minimum to the range high. Where an entry gets a band, a value above the range high is in range-d10 (Highest) unless it is below the minimum. The decile basis and band computation are stated on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page, proposed and pending ratification by the governance body.

resource.name: Nutrient Decile Bands
resource.description: The 14 bands of the Dynamic Decile System: four bands below the requirement minimum, as a share of the minimum, and ten deciles from the minimum to the range high. Where an entry gets a band, a value above the range high is in range-d10 unless it is below the minimum. The computation is stated, proposed and pending ratification, on the [Decile Basis and Band Computation](band-computation.html) page.

resource.name: Nutrient Decile Bands Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Nutrient Decile Bands code system.

resource.name: OAN Assessment Codes
resource.description: Codes for the kind of assessment an Open Animal Nutrition observation records.

resource.name: Requirement Standards
resource.description: Published nutrient requirement standards an adequacy check can be run against. Each standards body's code has a child code for each edition (is-a); record the edition's code when the edition is known. The editions are those the source template, Version 21OCT26b, cites.

resource.name: Requirement Standards Value Set
resource.description: All codes in the Requirement Standards code system: the standards bodies and their editions.
